title: Catalog controls for the AI licensing era

claimLedger.centralClaim: Labels and publishers can prepare catalog-specific AI licensing decisions and connect their reviewed recording and composition records through participating rights nodes.
strongestEvidence: Runnable synthetic tour with separate authority, policy, approval and receipt records
Two-node verifier covering signed discovery, consent, changed policy, withdrawal and partial failure
Container proof exercising the same API through the shipped web proxy
claimLedger.scopeAndLimits: Current local candidate; fictional example data; explicitly configured peers. Public release requires corresponding source and hosted acceptance. Organizations supply rights evidence. API policies describe inputs and reporting obligations; asset delivery, use monitoring and payments require operator integrations.
claimLedger.falsifier: An approval exceeds reviewed authority or current policy, a private record appears without party access, a source result cannot be verified, or the illustrated workflow requires an unimplemented capability.
claimLedger.whyItMatters: Organizations can offer defined AI uses while maintaining creator instructions, review accountability and the evidence behind catalog connections.

scenes.title: Your catalog, ready for AI licensing
scenes.narration: A label controls a recording. A publisher represents the song. Their artists and writers have conditions. Clef puts those decisions in one place, ready for your team and for licensing requests.
scenes.capture: Open the prepared example. Show the recording and composition cards together.

scenes.title: One title. Two sets of rights.
scenes.narration: This is Paper Skies by Mara Vale, a fictional artist. The recording and composition have separate identifiers and separate administrators. Each representative supplies evidence of the rights, share and territory it administers.
scenes.capture: Show the illustrative ISRC and ISWC, the separate organizations and their example mandates.

scenes.title: The creator sets the conditions
scenes.narration: Mara permits a short instrumental study using selected musical inputs. The example limits the source extract, the output, the model environment and retention. Training, vocals and other uses have their own choices. Your team can set those conditions across a catalog and review the terms of each request.
scenes.capture: Open artist choices. Show the current input choices, 30-second source limit, 60-second output limit and private model.

scenes.title: Review the exact use
scenes.narration: Now the studio requests the use. The recording and composition receive separate reviews. Approvals include the credit and reporting obligations. Try a broader territory or a request for model training: Clef checks it against the current conditions and authority.
scenes.capture: Approve each side, then submit the training and worldwide probes. Keep the response visible.

scenes.title: Keep the agreement verifiable
scenes.narration: Each approval produces a signed receipt. Authorized parties can inspect the original. Change its territory in a test copy and verification catches the alteration. Public receipts use a separate disclosure choice made before signing.
scenes.capture: Verify the original and an altered copy. Show both results; briefly show the private download and disclosure screen.

scenes.title: Connect participating catalogs
scenes.narration: In this local demonstration, a label and publisher run separate nodes. One search finds both records, with each source signing its own answer. Administrators choose the public fields and can withdraw a listing. Buyers can discover the conditions at the source.
scenes.capture: Search Paper Skies across the two local nodes. Show both origins, the matching identifiers, choices and signature status before expiry.

scenes.title: Build better catalog connections
scenes.narration: Labels contribute recording records. Publishers contribute composition records. The MLC adds U.S. publishing references and recording metadata supplied by streaming services. Your team reviews the connections and supplies its own rights evidence.
scenes.capture: Use a labeled source diagram: label recording records; publisher works and mandates; The MLC references; reviewed connection.

scenes.title: Start with a catalog
scenes.narration: Self-install Clef or have us set it up in your infrastructure. Start with a small catalog and your reviewers. The opportunity is more music ready for agreed AI uses, with creators’ conditions carried into each decision.
scenes.capture: Close on the setup paths and a small-catalog pilot invitation. Confirm every destination against the adopted release.
